Line 273: DoubleVector.Builder result = new DoubleVector.Builder();
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
was this necessary in the end?

you can simplify this code a bit by doing

sum += source.getElementAsDouble(i);
if(Double.isNaN(sum)) {
result.addNA();
} else {
result.add(sum);
}

the + operator will always give you the NaN if one of the operands is NaN,
the (potential problem) is that the NA marker is stripped and (1 + NA =
NaN) rather than NA.

For more information:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/detail?r=285
